title: Which clarifying questions should you ask at the start of a case?
description: The right question can split the whole case in two before you draw anything. What to do, what to say, and the mistake to avoid.
hook: Clarifying questions show you are thinking, but too many make you look unsure. Three at most is a good rule. Here is how to choose the ones that matter.
body:
Stage 3 of 10 in the ten stages of a case.

Why it matters

The right question can split the whole case in two before you draw anything.

The common mistake

Asking a long list of questions to buy time.

What to do, and what to say

Pick the questions that matter

Choose the 2-3 that matter most: business model, measurable goal and timeline, product mix, customers, geography, scope, suppliers.

"How does the client actually make money?" / "Is there a specific target and timeline for this goal?"

Ask to build, not to stall

Only ask a question if its answer would change what you draw next.

"Is this a problem the whole industry is facing, or just our client?"

Ask for thinking time

After your recap and questions, formally ask for time to structure.

"Thank you, that’s useful. May I take a moment to structure my thoughts?"

Practise the moment

Read the situation and say your answer out loud before you open the model.

You’ve recapped and asked your clarifying questions. You need time to think.

Show a strong answer

"Thank you, that’s useful. May I take a moment to structure my thoughts?"

Why it works: Silence is fine once you’ve asked for it.

A profitability case. Which single question splits the case in two?

Show a strong answer

"Is this a problem the whole industry is facing, or just our client?"

Why it works: Industry-wide points to the market; company-only points to the client’s own revenue or costs.

The prompt says the client "wants to grow" but gives no number. Ask about the goal.

Show a strong answer

"Is there a specific growth target, and a timeline attached to it?"

Why it works: A quantified goal is what you link every later answer back to.

You don’t understand how the client earns money (it’s a platform business).

Show a strong answer

"How does the client actually make money? Is it a commission on each transaction, a subscription, or advertising?"

Why it works: The business model decides how you split revenue in your structure.

Next stage: structure.
outro: Practise stage 3 with flashcards on the free perfect casing page. Next in this topic: How do you present your structure in a case interview?
